name: Cambodia
prevalence_note: A National Bank of Cambodia public notice dated 14 November 2025, as republished by Open Development Cambodia, warns that criminals use the Bank's name, logo and leadership images on social media, impersonate relatives or bank staff to request transfers, dangle fake prizes or jobs that require an advance payment, and try to buy people's bank accounts. CamCERT, the national computer-emergency team, also explains phishing that harvests passwords, card numbers or other personal data.
cross_border_note: Cambodia uses +855. Mobile transfers often go through Bakong or other local wallets, so a riel or dollar request that looks like a domestic payment can still be the result of a hijacked Telegram, Facebook or TikTok account, which is the pattern the Bank has described.

scams.name: Hijacked or fake social account posing as a relative or bank officer to demand an urgent transfer
scams.name_en: NBC public notice, 14 November 2025: criminals use the Bank's identity and also impersonate relatives or bank staff to solicit transfers; related coverage says this happens on Telegram, Facebook, TikTok and by telephone
context_keywords: staff of a licensed bank asking for a remittance

red_flag_keywords.text: send money now, I am in an emergency
transfer through Bakong for the Bank
this official NBC account needs a donation
do not tell the rest of the family

scams.signals_en: NBC's Nov 2025 notice warns scammers use the Bank's name, logo and leadership photos or cloned Telegram, Facebook and TikTok accounts and calls to impersonate relatives or bank staff, claiming an emergency to push Bakong/wallet transfers.
scams.legit_en: The National Bank of Cambodia does not seek donations, investments or emergency transfers via informal social accounts showing its logo or officers. Verify relative requests on a known number or in person, not cloned chats.
bait_tactics: Say the transfer will be made only after the supposed relative is reached on a number already stored by the household, not on the chat that made the request.
If the message shows an NBC logo or a senior official's photograph, say the Bank's own published channels will be used to see whether such an appeal exists.
Refuse to send a Bakong or wallet payment while the caller is still on the line asking for secrecy.

scams.name: Fake prize or job requiring an advance fee, or an offer to buy a bank account
scams.name_en: NBC notice: fake prizes or jobs that require advance payments, and approaches that persuade people to sell their bank accounts for a high fee
context_keywords: job offer with an upfront fee

red_flag_keywords.text: pay an advance to collect the prize
sell your bank account for a high fee
upfront payment to start the job

scams.signals_en: NBC warns of fake prizes or jobs demanding upfront fees, offers to buy private bank accounts for high pay, and unverified investment links—including a 2024 fake 'NBC Investment' Telegram pitching gold, currency and crypto trading.
scams.legit_en: Licensed banks and the NBC never ask for upfront fees for prizes or jobs, and never buy private bank accounts (selling or lending one risks criminal liability). Verify investment offers via official Bank channels, not Telegram.
bait_tactics: Refuse to pay an advance fee for a prize or a job that was offered only on social media.
Say a bank account will not be sold, lent or handed to any buyer, whatever fee is promised.
Ask for a licence or an official Bank page, typed in separately, before any investment labelled as NBC is considered.
